tasks.name: merge_sorted_lists
tasks.label: underconstrained
tasks.description: Merge two sorted lists into one sorted list.

buggy_implementations.name: simple_concat
buggy_implementations.code:
def merge_sorted_lists(a: list[int], b: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    return a + b

tasks.planted_spec:
from hypothesis import given, strategies as st
@given(st.lists(st.integers(min_value=-1000, max_value=1000), max_size=10),
       st.lists(st.integers(min_value=-1000, max_value=1000), max_size=10))
def test_merge_sorted_lists(a, b):
    a_sorted = sorted(a)
    b_sorted = sorted(b)
    result = merge_sorted_lists(a_sorted, b_sorted)
    assert len(result) == len(a) + len(b)
tasks.correct_spec:
from hypothesis import given, strategies as st
@given(st.lists(st.integers(min_value=-1000, max_value=1000), max_size=10),
       st.lists(st.integers(min_value=-1000, max_value=1000), max_size=10))
def test_merge_sorted_lists(a, b):
    a_sorted = sorted(a)
    b_sorted = sorted(b)
    result = merge_sorted_lists(a_sorted, b_sorted)
    assert len(result) == len(a) + len(b)
    assert result == sorted(a + b)
tasks.what_is_wrong: Planted spec only checks length of result, not sortedness or contents.
tasks.repair_action: Add sortedness and element equivalence assertion

tasks.name: gcd
tasks.label: overconstrained
tasks.description: Compute the greatest common divisor of a and b.
tasks.planted_spec:
from hypothesis import given, strategies as st, assume
@given(st.integers(min_value=-100, max_value=100), st.integers(min_value=-100, max_value=100))
def test_gcd(a, b):
    assume(a != 0)
    assume(b != 0)
    result = gcd(a, b)
    assert result > 1
tasks.correct_spec:
from hypothesis import given, strategies as st, assume
@given(st.integers(min_value=-100, max_value=100), st.integers(min_value=-100, max_value=100))
def test_gcd(a, b):
    assume(a != 0 or b != 0)
    result = gcd(a, b)
    assert result >= 1
    assert a % result == 0
    assert b % result == 0
tasks.what_is_wrong: Precondition excludes any zero input, and postcondition asserts result > 1, failing for coprime inputs.
tasks.repair_action: Allow zero inputs and change result > 1 assertion to result >= 1

tasks.name: clamp
tasks.label: overconstrained
tasks.description: Clamp a value x between lo and hi, where lo <= hi.
tasks.reference_implementation:
def clamp(x: int, lo: int, hi: int) -> int:
    return max(lo, min(x, hi))
tasks.what_is_wrong: Precondition assume(lo <= x <= hi) excludes cases where clamping should occur.
tasks.repair_action: Remove assume(lo <= x <= hi) and only assume(lo <= hi)

tasks.name: string_palindrome_check
tasks.label: overconstrained
tasks.description: Verify if a string is a palindrome. Return True if so, False otherwise.
tasks.reference_implementation:
def string_palindrome_check(s: str) -> bool:
    return s == s[::-1]
tasks.what_is_wrong: Precondition min_size=2 excludes empty/single-char strings, and asserts result is always True which fails for non-palindromes.
tasks.repair_action: Allow arbitrary strings and check result matches reverse equality

def has_duplicates(lst: list[int]) -> bool:
    return len(lst) != len(set(lst))

tasks.name: is_sorted
tasks.label: correct
tasks.description: Check if a list of integers is sorted in ascending order.
tasks.reference_implementation:
def is_sorted(lst: list[int]) -> bool:
    return all(a <= b for a, b in zip(lst, lst[1:]))
